question.text: Let $F(x)=3x^2-2x$ for $x\in[0,5),$ and let $f(x)$ be the odd extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in (-5,5).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in(-5,0)?$
question.explanation:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in[0,5),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} F(x), & x\in[0,5), \\[5pt] -F(-x), & x\in(-5,0). \end{cases} \]

In our case, for $x\in(-5,0),$ we get \begin{align*} f(x) &= -F(-x) \\[5pt] &= -(3(-x)^2-2(-x)) \\[5pt] &= -(3x^2+2x) \\[5pt] &= -3x^2-2x. \end{align*}

example.title: Understanding the Odd Extension of a Function

question.text: \[ f(x) \sim \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin(nx) \] Let $F(x)=-5x$ for $x\in[0,\pi).$ The Fourier sine series of the odd $2\pi$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for $b_n.$
question.explanation:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by \[ b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(nx)\,\text{d}x. \]

In our case, $f(x)=-5x$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get \[ b_n = -\dfrac{10}{\pi}\int_0^\pi x \sin(nx)\,\text{d}x. \]

We use the integration by parts: \begin{align*} u=x \qquad&\Rightarrow\qquad u' = 1 \\[3pt] v' = \sin(nx) \qquad&\Rightarrow\qquad v = -\dfrac{1}{n}\cos(nx) \end{align*}

Thus, we obtain \begin{align*} b_n &= -\dfrac{10}{\pi} \left( uv \, \Big|_0^\pi - \int_0^\pi vu' \,\text{d}x \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{10}{\pi} \left( -\dfrac{1}{n} \big[ x\cos(nx) \big]_{0}^{\pi} + \dfrac{1}{n} \int_0^\pi \cos(nx)\,\text{d}x \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10}{n\pi} \left( \left( \pi\cdot\cos(n\pi) - 0\cdot\cos(0) \right) - \dfrac{1}{n} \big[ \sin(nx) \big]_{0}^{\pi} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10}{n\pi} \left( \pi\cos(n\pi) - \dfrac{1}{n} \left( \sin(n\pi)-\sin(0) \right) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10\cos(n\pi)}{n}. \end{align*}

Finally, since $\cos(n\pi)=(-1)^n,$ we have \[ b_n = \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\dfrac{10(-1)^n}{n}}. \]

example.title: Computing the Sine Coefficients From the Half-Range Formula

question.text: Let $F(x)=7$ for $x\in[0,\pi).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the odd $2\pi$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.
question.explanation:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by \[ b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(nx)\,\text{d}x. \]

In our case, $f(x)=7$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} b_n &= \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi 7\sin(nx)\,\text{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{14}{\pi} \int_0^\pi \sin(nx)\,\text{d}x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{14}{n \pi} \big[ \cos(nx) \big]_0^\pi \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{14}{n \pi} \left( \cos(n\pi) - \cos(0) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{14(1-\cos(n\pi))}{n \pi}. \end{align*} Therefore, since $\cos(n\pi)=(-1)^n,$ we have \[ b_n = \dfrac{14(1-(-1)^n)}{\pi n}. \]

Finally, the Fourier sine series is \[ f(x) \sim \sum_{n=1}^\infty \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\dfrac{14(1-(-1)^n)}{\pi n}} \cdot \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\sin(nx)}. \]

example.title: Computing the Sine Coefficients From the Half-Range Formula

question.text: \[ f(x) \sim \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin(nx) \] Let $F(x)=-2x+3$ for $x\in[0,\pi).$ The Fourier sine series of the odd $2\pi$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for $b_n.$
question.explanation:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by \[ b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(nx)\,\text{d}x. \]

In our case, $f(x)=-2x+3$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get \[ b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi (-2x+3) \sin(nx)\,\text{d}x. \]

We use the integration by parts: \begin{align*} u=-2x+3 \qquad&\Rightarrow\qquad u' = -2 \\[3pt] v' = \sin(nx) \qquad&\Rightarrow\qquad v = -\dfrac{1}{n}\cos(nx) \end{align*}

Thus, we obtain \begin{align*} b_n &= \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left( uv \, \Big|_0^\pi - \int_0^\pi vu' \,\text{d}x \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left( -\dfrac{1}{n} \big[ (-2x+3)\cos(nx) \big]_{0}^{\pi} - \dfrac{2}{n} \int_0^\pi \cos(nx)\,\text{d}x \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{n\pi} \left( \left( (-2\pi+3)\cos(n\pi) - 3\cdot\cos(0) \right) + \dfrac{2}{n} \big[ \sin(nx) \big]_{0}^{\pi} \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{n\pi} \left( (-2\pi+3)\cos(n\pi)-3 + \dfrac{2}{n} \left( \sin(n\pi)-\sin(0) \right) \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{n\pi}\left((-2\pi+3)\cos(n\pi)-3\right). \end{align*}

Finally, since $\cos(n\pi)=(-1)^n,$ we have \[ b_n =-\dfrac{2}{n\pi}\left((-2\pi+3)(-1)^n-3\right)= \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\dfrac{2}{n\pi}\left((-1)^n(2\pi-3)+3\right)}. \]

question.text: Let $F(x)=x^2-2x$ for $x\in[0,10),$ and let $f(x)$ be the odd extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in (-10,10).$ What is the value of $f(-6)?$
question.explanation:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in[0,10),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} F(x), & x\in[0,10), \\[5pt] -F(-x), & x\in(-10,0). \end{cases} \]

In our case, for $x\in(-10,0),$ we get \begin{align*} f(x) &= -F(-x) \\[5pt] &= -((-x)^2-2(-x))\\[5pt] &= -(x^2+2x) \\[5pt] &= -x^2-2x. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} f(-6) &= -(-6)^2-2(-6)= \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{-24}. \end{align*}
